Dz is a digraph of the Latin script , consisting of the consonants D and Z . It generally represents / d͡z / in Latin alphabets, including Hungarian , Kashubian , Latvian , Lithuanian , Polish , Slovak , and romanized Macedonian . However, it represents / t͡s / in Chipewyan (Dënesųłinë́) and the ILE romanization of Cantonese , and is a pronunciation respelling of the letter D to represent /z/ in Vietnamese . [ 1 ]
